reason: The text describes a fundamental failure of collaboration between leaders and people. When the people petition King Rehoboam to ease their heavy burdens, he initially consults with elders who advise him: 'If you serve the people and speak kindly to them, they will be your servants forever.' This represents a path toward collaboration, but Rehoboam explicitly rejects this counsel. Instead, he listens to younger advisors and responds harshly to the people's plea, threatening even greater hardship ('My father laid a heavy yoke on you; I will add to your yoke'). As a direct result, the people rebel: they withdraw support from Rehoboam, declare they have no part in David's line, and rally to Jeroboam as king. The kingdom divides, and the text emphasizes ongoing conflict ('And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days'). Rather than collaboration and working together, the passage depicts the breakdown of the leader-people relationship and active conflict.
